title: SOLID and TRACE finite-thickness +Z wireframe fallback
scope: Extend the legacy-consumer fallback for canonical +Z SOLID/TRACE entities to expose finite signed thickness as a boundary wireframe.

facts: Group 210 is the extrusion direction, default (0,0,1).
A SOLID with the fourth corner equal to the third is triangular.

autodeskSolidThickness.fact: Thickness is the shape dimension along its normal vector direction, also called the extrusion direction.

facts: TRACE group 39 is optional thickness, default 0.
Group 210 is the extrusion direction, default (0,0,1).

implementation.behavior: For canonical +Z extrusion only, emit the base boundary and, for finite nonzero thickness, the translated top boundary plus unique vertical edges. Translation is along WCS Z because canonical +Z makes the OCS/WCS axes coincide. Signed thickness is preserved. Non-finite input/translated vertices fail closed for the extrusion portion; zero thickness keeps the existing planar fallback. Other extrusion normals remain on the typed callback path.
implementation.triangleBehavior: A repeated fourth/third corner emits no zero-length edge and no duplicate vertical edge.
limits: The fallback emits boundary LINE callbacks only; it does not encode filled faces or volume.
No independent native CAD rendering or file interoperability claim is made.
3D consumers should override addTrace/addSolid to receive the full typed record.

controls: positive thickness emits top and side edges
negative thickness follows the signed +Z extrusion
non-finite thickness omits the extrusion portion
triangular SOLID has nine unique boundary edges
presentation attributes and synthetic NoHandle identities are preserved

fixturePolicy: No DWG or DXF fixture was added.
